Ridge networks: effective penalty and edge selection

Source: vignettes/ridge-networks.Rmd
ridge-networks.Rmd

The ridge precision estimator (S+λI)−1(S + \lambda I)^{-1} has no zero entries. For Gaussian data its partial correlations estimate those of (Σ+κI)−1(\Sigma + \kappa I)^{-1}, where the effective penalty κ\kappa exceeds λ\lambda (Arashi and Ebrahim, 2026, submitted). This vignette shows how to estimate κ\kappa and how to select edges. These functions come from the package ridgegraph by Mohammad Arashi.

library(ebrahim.gof)
set.seed(1)
p <- 30; n <- 20
theta <- diag(p)
for (i in 1:(p - 1)) theta[i, i + 1] <- theta[i + 1, i] <- 0.4
x <- matrix(rnorm(n * p), n, p) %*% chol(solve(theta))
effective_penalty(x, c(0.05, 0.5, 5))
#>   lambda  df_ratio      scale    kappa
#> 1   0.05 0.9232675 0.07673254 0.651614
#> 2   0.50 0.6788698 0.32113025 1.557001
#> 3   5.00 0.2748789 0.72512113 6.895400
effective_penalty_floor(x)
#> [1] 0.4619051

With p>np > n the effective penalty does not fall below the floor however small λ\lambda is. Edges can be selected with the permutation threshold.

sel <- mps_select(x, B = 99)
sum(sel$adjacency[upper.tri(sel$adjacency)])
#> [1] 1
